hook: Leo has \$12 for lunch at a food festival. Tacos are \$2 and smoothies are \$4. The first smoothie is great; the third is fine; a fifth taco would barely register. He does not need a formula to feel this, but the exam asks for one: spend each dollar where it adds the most satisfaction, and stop when one more unit adds less than it costs.

options: total benefit minus the full cost
total benefit plus the full cost
prereq.why: Subtract every cost from the benefit.

prereq.q: Jamal's net benefit is \$45 at 3 lessons and \$40 at 4. Taking the fourth lesson
options: adds more to cost than to benefit
adds more to benefit than to cost
prereq.why: Net benefit falls, so the extra cost is larger.

figure.caption: Leo's marginal utility for tacos (\$2) and smoothies (\$4), and per dollar. With \$12, the best bundle is 2 tacos and 2 smoothies: the last of each gives 8 per dollar, and total utility is 116. Invented data for practice.

chain.cause: A consumer eats more units of a good
chain.effect: each extra unit adds less satisfaction than the one before (diminishing marginal utility)
the consumer compares marginal utility per dollar, MU ÷ P, not marginal utility alone

chain.cause: One good gives more utility per dollar than another
chain.effect: moving a dollar toward it raises total utility

chain.cause: The budget is spent and MU per dollar is equal across goods
chain.effect: no move can raise total utility: the consumer has the utility-maximizing bundle

ideas: Marginal analysis: decide one more unit at a time. Do one more unit when its marginal benefit is at least its additional cost; stop when it is less.
Utility is satisfaction. Marginal utility (MU) is the extra utility from one more unit, and it usually falls as you consume more: diminishing marginal utility.
Utility-maximizing rule: spend the whole budget so that $\frac{\text{MU}_X}{P_X} = \frac{\text{MU}_Y}{P_Y}$. Buy each next unit where MU per dollar is highest.
The budget constraint limits the bundles a consumer can afford: spending on all goods cannot exceed income.
A sunk cost is already spent and cannot be recovered. It is the same whatever you choose next, so it never changes the best choice.

misconception.wrong: Leo should buy smoothies first and keep buying them, because each smoothie gives more utility than any taco.
misconception.right: Smoothies cost twice as much. Compare MU per dollar: the first smoothie gives 12 per dollar, but the second gives 8, the same as the second taco. With \$12 the best bundle is 2 tacos and 2 smoothies (total utility 116), not 3 smoothies (104).

summary: Marginal analysis compares the extra benefit of one more unit with its extra cost: keep going while the marginal benefit is at least the additional cost. Consumers get utility from goods, and marginal utility usually diminishes as they consume more. With a budget, a consumer maximizes total utility by buying the next unit with the highest marginal utility per dollar until the budget is spent and MU ÷ P is equal across goods. Sunk costs are already paid whatever you choose, so they never change the best decision.
